verses.text: As the number of disciples kept growing, the Greek-speaking believers complained about the Hebrew-speaking believers. Their widows were being overlooked in the daily food distribution.
The Twelve called all the disciples together and said, “It wouldn’t be right for us to leave God’s message behind just to serve meals.
So, brothers and sisters, choose seven men from among you who are respected, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom. We’ll put them in charge of this work.
Then we can stay focused on prayer and serving God’s message.”
The whole group liked that plan. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit; Philip; Prochorus; Nicanor; Timon; Parmenas; and Nicolaus, a convert to Judaism from Antioch.
They brought these seven to the apostles, who prayed and placed their hands on them.
God’s message kept spreading. The number of disciples in Jerusalem grew fast, and a large number of priests accepted the faith.
Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and signs among the people.
But some members of the synagogue called the Freedmen—along with people from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and Asia—started arguing with Stephen.
They couldn’t stand up to the wisdom and the Spirit behind what he was saying.
So they secretly persuaded some men to say, “We heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and God.”
They stirred up the people, the elders, and the legal experts. Then they rushed Stephen, seized him, and brought him before the council.
They brought in false witnesses who said, “This man never stops speaking blasphemous words against this holy place and the Law.
We heard him say that Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses passed down to us.”
Everyone sitting on the council stared at Stephen. His face looked like an angel’s.
